_note: What Shino, the indigo dyer of Minamino, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items her own answers to a paper fan and to dishes. Mornings at the vats she talks of the dyeing. The birthday lines (winter 4), the close lines from band 4, the pattern lines once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_shino_5), the dear lines at band 6 once her band 6 scene is (heart_shino_6) until she is promised; engaged_ lines once she said yes to the knot, and married (married_shino) help_ lines on a morning she did a chore, wed_morning_ / wed_evening_ at the farmhouse and wed_out_ elsewhere (data/marriage.json). She speaks plainly and briefly. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Cherry blossoms are the hardest pink to dye. The tree makes it look easy. I'm a little jealous.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Half the yukata here are from our vats. Mother's patterns, my dipping. Look at the hems.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Moonlight turns indigo almost black. This is the one night my cloth looks the way I see it in my head.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A new year. The vats have to be fed tonight too. Indigo doesn't take holidays.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Again? Then hand me that pole. Visitors stir.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: You'll go home blue if you keep standing this close to the vats.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: You're the new farmer. Shino. I dye indigo. Don't shake my hand, it's blue to the wrist.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I came back from the city last spring. Everyone asks why. The vats asked first.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Rain means the vats inside. The smell gets into the tatami. I've stopped noticing.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Dip, lift, let the air turn it blue. Again. Twenty times for a good dark. Don't count, it's bad luck.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The vat's in a good mood today. See the copper skin on top? That's called the flower.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Rinsing. The river takes the loose dye downstream. Mio says her fish look bluer since I came home.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Cold water makes the clearest blue. My hands disagree. They're the clearest blue too.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: In the city they dye a thousand shirts in an hour. One color. No smell. No life in it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Kiku brings me persimmon skins to try. Orange, she hopes. So far it's been brown. She's patient.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Mother kept the vats alive thirty years. I've kept them alive one. They forgive me so far.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: You remembered? Then I'll tell you a secret. The vats get the day off on my birthday. I sit by the river and do nothing.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: For my birthday? ...Mother used to give me one plain white cloth each year, to dye however I liked. This feels the same.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I dyed a cloth the color of your field after rain. Dark, almost green. Don't ask to buy it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: People in the city talked a lot and said little. You're the other way round. I like it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I cut a new stencil last night. Then another. My fingers are full of tiny cuts. Worth it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Sayo put my first new cloth in the store window. Somebody asked who made it. She pointed at me.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I keep finding reasons to stand at the vats facing your road. The light's better. That's my story.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The darkest blue takes the most dips. I think people are the same. You've had a lot of dips with me.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Kiku says I hum at the vats now. I never hummed in the city. Not once.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I'm dyeing my own wedding sash. Three days isn't enough dips. I'll make it enough.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Mother would have said the vat knew before I did. It's been strangely calm all week.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Morning. There's tea. My hands left blue prints on your cup. Our cup.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Off to the vats. If you come by at noon, bring rice balls. I forget to eat when the color's right.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I hung a new noren on the door while you slept. Indigo, of course. What else.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Welcome home. You smell of soil. I smell of vat. We match.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Sit. Let me mend your sleeve. And dye it, while I'm at it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: In the city the nights were loud. Here I can hear the frogs and you. That's all I want to hear.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I watered the dry plots before the vats. Plants want water the way cloth wants dye.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The rows by the path were thirsty, so I gave them a can. Now they're greener than my best dye.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I filled the coop's feed box. The hens stared at my hands. They've never seen a blue farmer.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: The feed's in the coop, from your sack. Feeding hens is easier than feeding a vat.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Married, and still blue to the wrist. Some things don't change. Good.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Kiku asks if I'm eating. I tell her someone at home makes sure of it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Oh. Look at this color. I'm going to try it in the vat tonight. Thank you.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: That's good. Thank you.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: For me? Thank you.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Hm. Not for me, I'm afraid. Thanks anyway.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A stone. Gray, too. The one color I can't stand.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Another? One a day is plenty. Keep it for tomorrow.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A painted fan. Look how they did the waves. I'm going to steal this pattern. Respectfully.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: You cooked this? It smells like home used to. Thank you.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Still warm. I'll eat it by the vats.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A dish. Thank you, that's supper sorted.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Too sweet for me. I had enough of that in the city. Sorry.
